The phrase "हज़रत मुहम्मद और ख़दीजा की पुत्री अली की पत्नी" seems to be a description: "the daughter of Hazrat Muhammad and Khadija, Ali's wife". Actually "हज़रत मुहम्मद और ख़दीजा की पुत्री" = daughter of Muhammad and Khadija, i.e., Fatima. Then "अली की पत्नी" = wife of Ali. So the entity is Fatima (Fatima Zahra). Then "हसन और हुसैन की मां थीं" = mother of Hasan and Husayn.

Thus the pronoun "वे" refers to "हज़रत मुहम्मद और ख़दीजा की पुत्री अली की पत्नी, हसन और हुसैन की मां". The entity is described fully after "वे". The pronoun is at start, and the rest of sentence defines who they are. The entity is not named elsewhere before pronoun; it's defined after pronoun. The rule: "entity that pronoun refers to is named somewhere else in the SAME sentence." Here the entity is described after pronoun, but is that considered "named"? The phrase "यह अभयारण्य" includes the noun "अभयारण्य". The pronoun "यह" refers to the same noun, but the entity is not named elsewhere besides the noun itself. The rule: "entity that pronoun refers to is named somewhere else in the SAME sentence." Here the entity is "अभयारण्य". It is present as part of the phrase "यह अभयारण्य". But is that considered "named elsewhere"? The pronoun "यह" is a demonstrative, not a proper name. The entity is "अभयारण्य" which is a common noun, not a proper name. The instruction: "named somewhere else in the SAME sentence." In examples, they replace pronoun with the entity name. Example: "पूरा शहर ... और यह 111 फुट..." replaced "यह" with "शहर". They used the noun "शहर" which appears earlier. So they used the noun that appears earlier. Here "यह अभयारण्य". The noun "अभयारण्य" appears right after pronoun. So we can replace "यह" with "अभयारण्य". The resulting sentence: "अभयारण्य अभयारण्य घने वन के लिए जाना जाता है, जिसमें 30 मीटर तक के वृक्ष हैं।" That sounds odd: duplication.
